findings.title: Missing ENV now defaults to local auth bypass
findings.problem: The Dockerfile no longer sets ENV=development; the value now lives only in .env.standalone(.example), loaded via compose env_file. If the container starts without ENV (stale .env.standalone created before this change, docker run without env_file, or the line deleted), the backend default ENV=local (config.py:52) applies. Nothing in the entrypoint validates ENV, despite its header comment promising env validation.
findings.impact: In local mode the backend accepts a user-id header as login and treats every user as admin (security/user.py:93, idp/local.py:84), so an upgrade with an old env file silently yields an auth-bypassed deployment. The README only asks users to copy three lines manually. Reachability confirmed through compose env_file wiring; severity capped at major because the example file and README warn about it.
findings.recommendation: Fail fast in the entrypoint before starting uvicorn when ENV is unset or `local` (e.g. [ "${ENV:-local}" = "local" ] && { echo 'ERROR: ENV must be set and not local; see .env.standalone.example' >&2; exit 1; }), or restore an image-level ENV=development default. No spec exists to settle which the owner prefers; the newly introduced ambiguity is kept blocking.
